review_kind: fresh independent Phase 0 adversarial review of v7 field-adjacency ledger

reviewer.lens: ADR exact grammar/actual supplied-field adjacency, public seams, and no-effect authority

scope_checked: all v7 L/C rows, profiles, actual schema operands, retained grammar, suffix/signature/revocation, and deliberate absences
all 0049/0050 corrections and public ReleaseKeyring/TrustedClock-only no-effect seam

findings.invariant: A complete field-adjacency successor must retain v6's exact closed grammar, not replace it with an unenumerated local-check bucket.
findings.evidence: L01 says only ‘all named schema literals, scalar types, arrays, ordering ... roles/uses’; 0051.shapes is merely comma-separated field names. It omits the actual schema/literal/type tables, ActionId set, replay-set cardinality, AuthorityRef alternatives, array keys, and per-envelope role/use matrix that 0048 explicitly supplied. No v7 rule identifies which constant each field must equal.
findings.worked_counterexample: A preflight built from v7 can accept an arbitrary ActionIntent.schema, an arbitrary ActionIntentSet membership, or a CES issuer_role/key_usage while satisfying canonical parsing, the listed key names, self digest, signature, and every C01-C24 comparator; selecting the v6/ADR literal is not implementable from the v7 record.
findings.consequence: The claimed exhaustive ledger is both an overbroad grouped row and a regression in retained grammar: valid inputs are ambiguous and invalid grammar can pass. This defeats Packet 3's closed-schema/signature objective before any adjacency check.
findings.required_correction: Carry forward the complete v6 closed-shape, scalar/literal, array-sort, signed-suffix role/use, and profile tables verbatim (or an equally explicit per-envelope replacement), then make L01 enumerate only the precise local fields it owns. Preserve C01-C24 as additional explicit comparisons.

findings.invariant: CES entries must be an exact, source-kind-correct binding of the selected intent's captured published-input contracts; a predecessor-output contract cannot be admitted as a CES/PCE capture and no required published-input contract may be omitted or repeated.
findings.evidence: C22 gives only CES-entry -> ‘exactly one’ selected InputContract comparison of four fields. It neither requires InputContract.source_kind == published-input nor the reverse/cardinality direction. Thus required_input_contracts has no exhaustive CES disposition; C15 governs predecessor edges but does not repair C22's one-way relation.
findings.worked_counterexample: For a selected action, supply two distinct CES entries with the same binding_id/node/input/purpose and different valid phase-PIS PublishedInputEntry values, while omit a second required published-input contract; each entry selects that first contract and C23/C24 mirror both into CAS. Alternatively select a predecessor-output contract with those four fields. All named v7 rows pass, but the tuple captures an extra/wrong port and omits a declared required input.
findings.consequence: A directly supplied input-contract/port substitution remains locally admissible, contradicting ADR's closed input-contract, CES/PCE projection, and missing/extra capture refusal requirements.
findings.required_correction: Require a bijection between CES entries and exactly the selected child contracts with source_kind published-input: each such contract occurs once with binding_id/consumer_node/consumer_input/purpose equal; predecessor-output contracts have no CES entry and retain C15's edge/ref rules. Keep source_ref syntax-only because the tuple has no peer encoding.

assessment.prior_corrections: 0049 M01-M03 and 0050 M01-M03 are individually represented by C02/C15/C18-C24 and C08-C13, subject to the two open completeness failures above.
assessment.public_interface: trust.py publicly exposes ReleaseKeyring and TrustedClock; verifier.py currently exposes only the Packet-2 HistoricalStudyVerifier/CaptureDriver facades. v7 correctly proposes no use of LifecycleAuthority or a private trust helper.
assessment.no_effect_boundary: Still correctly non-authorizing in intent: no resolver, capture, session, WORM, admission consumption, import, construction, execution, or deployment is authorized. The open findings require docs-only contract repair, not a runtime expansion.

summary.reason: v7 fixes prior named links but loses the executable closed grammar and omits a bidirectional CES-to-input-contract/source-kind binding.

required_next_gate: Repair both Major families in a successor docs-only matrix, retain all explicit prior links and no-effect limits, then obtain a fresh independent Phase-0 review; RED remains false.
